sources.title: Story-Based Inquiry: A Manual for Investigative Journalists, second edition
sources.publisher: UNESCO / Mark Lee Hunter and contributors
sources.supports: Provisional hypotheses, event chronology and source-linked editorial checking.
sources.limitations: Actual 188-page PDF obtained from author-linked public download. Read selected chapter 2, 3 and 8 passages, not the whole book. PDF frontmatter says 2026; author landing page says 2025.

sources.title: Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations
sources.publisher: OHCHR / UC Berkeley Human Rights Center
sources.supports: Preservation and verification of source, digital item and content; independent corroboration.
sources.limitations: Read selected preservation, verification, analysis and bias paragraphs, especially 161–200. Human-rights protocol; its procedural safeguards do not establish any allegation here.

sources.title: Causal Inference: What If — January 2025 revision
sources.publisher: Miguel A. Hernán / James M. Robins, author-hosted book
sources.supports: Distinguishing confounding from selection bias; conditions for identifying causal effects.
sources.limitations: Read selected chapters 7 and 8 in the full author PDF. No causal effect estimated for this project. Book examples are mainly epidemiological.

sources.title: A Guide to Fact-Checking Investigative Stories
sources.supports: Line-by-line checking, contrary evidence and attention to the narrative frame.
sources.limitations: Professional practice guidance, not a controlled validation study. Published responses can be checked; contacting subjects requires authorization.

sources.title: OpenSanctions Pairs: Large-Scale Entity Matching with LLMs
sources.publisher: Smith, Sesodia, Lindenberg and Schroeder de Witt / arXiv
sources.supports: Pairwise entity matching evaluation and errors involving identifiers, scripts and incomplete records.
sources.limitations: Read dataset, matching, evaluation and limitation sections. Candidate pairs are selected by blocking; labels reflect analyst decisions. Pairwise results do not validate entire graphs or Indian registries.

sources.title: Time to Reflect: Can We Trust LLM Judges for Evidence-based Research Agents?
sources.supports: Testing evaluators with controlled errors in research trajectories and evidence use.
sources.limitations: Read task construction, judge setup and limitations. Synthetic perturbations do not cover all naturally occurring failures; no local benchmark reproduced.

sources.title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability, version 3
sources.supports: Reliability dimensions beyond average task success: consistency, robustness, predictability and failure severity.
sources.limitations: Read abstract, framework and evaluation overview, not every appendix. Results concern the studied tasks and models; they do not establish reliability for this investigation.

sources.title: The Psychology of Conspiracy Theories
sources.publisher: Douglas, Sutton and Cichocka / Current Directions in Psychological Science
sources.supports: Review of epistemic, existential and social motives relevant to investigator self-scrutiny.
sources.limitations: Read the article text in the author repository PDF. Population-level research cannot diagnose individuals or decide whether a particular allegation is true.

sources.title: Offshore Leaks Database: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.supports: Dataset-specific coverage, transformations, duplicate identities and derived similar-name/address links.
sources.limitations: Read FAQ sections on coverage, transformations and interpretation. Database presence is not evidence of an offence; records are historical and incomplete.

sources.title: Beneficial Ownership Data Standard 0.4: Key Concepts
sources.supports: Separating source assertions from real-world facts and keeping dated, append-only ownership statements.
sources.limitations: Read concepts page, not complete schema or jurisdictional ownership law. A conforming record can still contain an inaccurate declaration.

sources.title: OpenSanctions: Statement Data Model
sources.supports: Field-level source lineage and separate source and canonical identifiers.
sources.limitations: Read full page. First/last observed dates are pipeline observations; they need not be the dates a relationship legally began or ended. Licensing must be checked before reuse.

sources.title: OpenSanctions: Identifiers and Deduplication
sources.supports: Canonical ID changes, merge/split history and limits of consolidated profiles.
sources.limitations: Read full page. Vendor documentation describes its system, not validated accuracy for a local importer; software openness and dataset permissions differ.

sources.title: Process Tracing: From Metaphor to Analytic Tool, chapter 1
sources.publisher: Andrew Bennett / Jeffrey T. Checkel, Cambridge University Press
sources.supports: Publisher summary identifies competing causal mechanisms as the book chapter’s concern.
sources.limitations: Publisher summary and bibliographic record read only. SFU working-paper link denied access and another author chapter timed out; no claim to have read those chapters.

sources.title: Suspicious conspiracy theories
sources.supports: Distinguishing reasons to prioritize investigation from evidence that establishes or refutes a particular theory.
sources.limitations: Publisher full text opened; introduction and sections 6–8 inspected. A philosophical argument in an active debate, not an empirical accuracy benchmark or endorsement of a current allegation.

methods.title: Opposing hypotheses and discriminating observations
methods.purpose: Turn a suspicion into a question that can lose against an ordinary or alternative explanation.
steps: Define actor, action, relevant period, alleged mechanism and the exact observation requiring explanation.
Before broad searching, write at least one plausible lawful explanation, a competing misconduct mechanism and an error or missing-record explanation.
For each hypothesis specify an observable consequence, a contrary observation, and whether a public record should exist and be discoverable.
Record what evidence changed the assessment. Preserve rejected hypotheses; do not explain away every contrary fact as concealment.
failureModes: Vague allegations that cannot fail
Treating missing evidence as confirmation without a discoverability argument
Using psychology to dismiss a specific documented claim
methods.benchmarkLimits: Procedural safeguard; this project has not benchmarked its effect on investigative accuracy.

methods.title: Source, item and content verification
methods.purpose: Keep exactly what was acquired separate from what the investigator inferred.
steps: Log requested and final URL, publisher, retrieval time, response status and actual access depth; treat an index as an index.
Where permitted, preserve acquired bytes with SHA-256, MIME type and version; keep extraction/OCR as separate derivatives with tool versions.
Inspect the cited passage or table in context, including page numbering, units, footnotes and scope.
Assign a source family to dependent reproductions. Multiple copies of the same filing count as one evidentiary origin.
Describe authenticity, factual accuracy and completeness separately; official publication does not automatically settle all three.
failureModes: Calling snippets full text
Hashing a derivative while claiming it is the original
Citation laundering through copied articles
methods.benchmarkLimits: Procedural safeguard; this project has not benchmarked its effect on investigative accuracy.

methods.title: Reversible entity resolution
methods.purpose: Prevent same-name records and changing corporate roles from creating false bridges.
steps: Retain raw names, source IDs, jurisdiction and valid time before normalization or transliteration.
Generate candidate matches, then adjudicate using identifiers and corroborating attributes; keep contradictions and an unresolved option.
Review the entire proposed cluster, including incompatible identifiers and simultaneous roles, before merging.
Version every merge and split. Test held-out names, scripts, source families and periods rather than reusing all training examples.
failureModes: Name-only or shared-address joins
Treating a score as an identity fact
Pairwise matches creating an inconsistent cluster
methods.benchmarkLimits: Pairwise benchmark results are not full-pipeline or network accuracy. The current literature informs design; this project has not reproduced a benchmark.

methods.title: Typed and dated connection paths
methods.purpose: Make each visible connection say exactly what a source establishes.
steps: Represent assertions with a precise predicate such as director-of, shareholding, award-to or paid-to; preserve source wording.
Keep event date, assertion date, filing date, retrieval date and valid interval distinct. Store partial dates as intervals, not invented days.
Test whether every edge in a proposed mechanism has the required date overlap, direction and legal entity identity.
Display unresolved bridge edges as questions. A path via an intermediary or registered agent does not itself establish control or money flow.
failureModes: Ownership inferred from directorship
Current role applied retrospectively
Derived similarity edge promoted to documented relationship
methods.benchmarkLimits: Procedural safeguard; this project has not benchmarked its effect on investigative accuracy.

methods.title: Comparison cohorts and causal identification
methods.purpose: Distinguish selected examples from evidence of a systematic differential outcome.
steps: Define unit, population, period, exposure, outcome and inclusion rule before selecting notable cases.
Acquire the eligible denominator, including unsuccessful bids, unexposed firms and records with missing outcomes; report coverage by stratum.
Draw a causal diagram separately from the entity graph, including common causes and the process deciding which records become visible.
Check temporal order, comparability, overlap and outcome measurement before estimating effects. Choose controls from the mechanism rather than predictive convenience.
If identification assumptions or data coverage cannot be defended, report descriptive associations and an acquisition plan instead of a causal estimate.
failureModes: Winner-only samples
Selection on investigated or highly publicized cases
Controlling for consequences of the alleged influence
methods.benchmarkLimits: Procedural safeguard; this project has not benchmarked its effect on investigative accuracy.

methods.title: Strategic predictions as acquisition tests
methods.purpose: Use incentives to identify discriminating records without treating a plausible story as proof.
steps: List institutional roles, available lawful choices, information and incentives using public evidence; label unknown payoffs.
Compare a compliant process, administrative failure and a hypothetical abuse at a high level; do not produce operational instructions for wrongdoing.
Derive different expected records for each model, then seek both supporting and contradicting records.
Identify the exact rule and jurisdiction from a current authoritative text before saying conduct would violate it. Distinguish allegation, finding and final disposition.
failureModes: Invented payoffs presented as equilibrium
Motive treated as action
Retrospective prediction fitted to a known outcome
methods.benchmarkLimits: This is a proposed synthesis for record acquisition, not a calibrated game-theoretic model or a method proven to discover conspiracies.

methods.title: Independent evidence review
methods.purpose: Give reviewers a chance to find wrong joins, unsupported wording and omitted context.
steps: A coordinator provides a fresh reviewer raw records and neutral questions, without the claimant agent’s proposed conclusion.
Require the reviewer to reconstruct cited amounts, dates and predicates and identify what each record cannot support.
Compare the independent result with the draft and resolve disagreements against records, retaining unresolved disputes.
Run a separate line-by-line review of public language, including allegation status, contrary material, scope and published responses.
failureModes: Role-play critics inheriting the same conclusion
Judging prose quality instead of evidence sufficiency
Calling agents independent sources
methods.benchmarkLimits: Context separation reduces one source of anchoring but does not make models statistically independent or guarantee error detection.

methods.title: Failure-oriented agent evaluation
methods.purpose: Measure whether the workflow catches important errors under modest perturbation.
steps: Create a held-out packet with a known source locator error, conflicting entity identifier, unit error or superseded document.
Keep the expected result outside the worker’s prompt. Ask it to perform the ordinary research task.
Score missed errors, false accusations, unsupported joins, source fidelity and appropriate abstention separately from task completion.
Repeat only to address a concrete reliability risk; report the small sample and avoid an overall accuracy claim.
failureModes: Evaluating only fluent final reports
Leaking expected answers into the review prompt
Synthetic success generalized to unseen cases
methods.benchmarkLimits: A local forward test is a smoke test. Neither these preprints nor a handful of tests establish investigative accuracy across sectors.

methods.title: Bounded acquisition and explicit gaps
methods.purpose: Turn an unresolved claim into a reproducible next record search.
steps: Choose the record with the highest ability to distinguish hypotheses; name its expected custodian, period and fields.
Enumerate official indexes and public links, search precise titles and variants, and log accessible, unavailable and irrelevant results.
Stop when the specified link set and query variants are exhausted or a decisive record resolves the question; state the boundary of the search.
Draft an optional formal request if needed, but send no message, request or login action without authorization.
failureModes: Claiming absence across all records from a limited search
Repeating broad searches without a new test
Using inaccessible records as if read
requiredOutputs: Next job with measurable success criteria
methods.benchmarkLimits: Procedural safeguard; this project has not benchmarked its effect on investigative accuracy.
